facts.text: Long before settlers, the area that is now Westwood, Iowa, hosted indigenous peoples, with prehistoric evidence found in the southeast Iowa woodlands.
In 1956, the first modern house appeared on Westwood Drive amid thick brush, marking the start of organized community planning.
Westwood officially incorporated on January 14, 1982, becoming a 48‑home wooded residential community known for its natural setting and wildlife.
A local history book edited by Wyn Seeley was published in 2018, offering a comprehensive record of Westwood’s founding and evolution for residents.
Westwood’s 0.15‑square‑mile community features a city‑maintained pond stocked with bass and bluegill, drawing migratory Canada geese and supporting local biodiversity.
Mid‑20th‑century archaeological digs uncovered an ossuary of five individuals—three adults and two juveniles—dating to the time of Christ, linked to Woodland period cultures.
